Different models and task, but the claim is about the shape of the curve, which is less tied to model size than the score is. If it holds, a class needs one good rewrite, not many.

Our tables are short, where the gap may be smaller than on WTQ-L.

But its check is a test suite, which says whether an answer is right; our checks (type, choices, non-answers) only say whether it is well formed, and E-17b showed a weak check lets wrong cheap answers through. The collapse was task-dependent on an 8B model, and nothing about a smaller one makes a typed question about its own thinking more reliable. This is the observer the note says has the weakest evidence, so E-04 puts it last.

A property of temperature scaling, not of the model's size, so it should hold here. E-04a fits one temperature per slice and left BANKING77 (77 options) out, so it neither tests nor depends on it yet; it matters as soon as one temperature is shared across tasks with different option counts.
A limit of one forward pass, not of model size, so it should hold for a small model too. Consistent but not a test: E-04a's untuned readout was already far below Jev on MedQA, MedMCQA and MMLU-Pro.

A failure out of distribution is a property of training on few labels, not of the answering model, so it should hold here; E-04 is to separate slices in and out of the training distribution for this reason.

The method does not depend on our generative models: BGE-small and logistic regression run cheaply on any hardware, so the conditions that differ are only the tasks and the labels. Against it: we have no labels yet, and arXiv 2605.02241 saw the same kind of classifier fall out of distribution (zsconf-embedding-router-ood).

Zero-shot and measured on 7 to 8B models, the nearest size class of any claim here. E-04a's readout margin is the same kind of signal and costs nothing extra (the note's E-04 step 2). The AUROC is modest, and our questions are typed decisions, not MMLU-Pro and TriviaQA answers.

Training-free, and its first-stage signal held down to 0.6B, so our models' size is not the obstacle. Against it: the gains are on Qwen3 and DeepSeek-V3.2 with their own thinking modes; our slow model is Inkling 2 Mini at Q4_K on llama.cpp, and E-04's questions are typed decisions, not those benchmarks; the numbers are the method's authors' own. Code is released (js-lee-AI/DART), so the paper's own number can be reproduced first.
